title: Lesson 59 - OmniStudio Governance: Development, Testing, and Deployment Processes
description: Recommend practices for establishing an effective governance model for development, testing, and deployment processes, including change management and documentation standards for Omnistudio artifacts.

questions.question: A team is about to edit an OmniScript directly in production to fix a quick issue. What is the correct governance response?
options: Allow it because it is fast and declarative
Reject it and require the change to go through a sandbox and a deployment gate
Allow it but log the change manually
Allow it only for Integration Procedures
questions.explanation: Direct production edits bypass review, testing, and rollback, so the correct response is to reject it and require the change to flow through a sandbox and a deployment gate. Allowing it, even with manual logging, still lacks the controlled process. Restricting the exception to Integration Procedures does not address the risk for OmniScripts.

questions.question: An architect is defining the test plan for a new Integration Procedure that writes to an external system. What must the plan cover?
options: External calls, payloads, and failure handling, plus the security context
Only the build, since it is declarative
Only the OmniScript that calls it
questions.explanation: An Integration Procedure that writes externally must be tested for its external calls, payloads, and failure handling, and for its security context, because those are where it can fail or expose data. Testing only the happy path misses the error cases. Testing only the build ignores behavior. Testing only the calling OmniScript ignores the IP's own behavior.

questions.question: A team wants to apply the same review depth to every OmniStudio artifact. What is the problem with this approach?
options: It is too strict for low-risk artifacts and too light for high-risk ones
It is the only fair way to govern
It eliminates the need for version control
questions.explanation: A one-size review depth either overburdens low-risk artifacts or underprotects high-risk ones, so the process is not proportionate to risk. It is not the only fair way; proportionate governance is more effective. It does not make deployments faster, and it does not replace version control.
